analysis.title: The Flow Show: Midterms, Bidterms, Skidterms
key_insights: BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 8.1 from 8.8, still in 'Sell' territory (sell above 8.0). The decline reflects weaker global stock index breadth and wider spreads in HY bonds and subordinated bank debt. Global stocks are up a modest 1.7% since the sell signal on May 26.
Weekly flows: $166.4bn to cash (largest since Apr 2020), $33.8bn to bonds, $12.4bn to stocks, $2.0bn to gold, $0.6bn out of crypto. Money market fund AUM is about $8tn, up from $5tn in 2023.

BofA says cash on the sidelines stays there until large monetary easing (QE1 in 2009, QE4 in 2020) or sustained Fed cuts: 'no rate cuts, no cash cuts'. MMFs earn about $330bn a year in interest with the T-bill yield at 4.2%.

Net 50% of global equity indices are 'oversold' (below both 50-day and 200-day moving averages), the most since Apr 2025. The contrarian buy signal needs net 88% and is unlikely soon unless the tech-heavy US, Taiwan and Korea indices reverse quickly.

BofA leans risk-off into the US midterms. Reasons: a central bank tightening cycle (54 hikes in 2026), tighter financial conditions, and credit 'canaries' (AUDJPY, risk parity, tech CDS such as ORCL and SOFTB). It notes recent investor hedging against a sharp drop.

Midterms are called the most likely catalyst for a +/-10% move in stocks into 2027. Polymarket odds: Democratic sweep 64% (up from 49% in September), GOP Senate/Dem House 28%, GOP sweep 9%. Trump approval is 38% (economy 34%, inflation 27%).

Scenario map. Dem sweep: stocks fall more than 10%, dollar and bond yields fall into year-end, international stocks beat the US and Europe beats Asia, with tax and regulation risk rising. GOP Senate/Dem House ('gridlock = Goldilocks'): stocks up more than 5%, positive for tech and the dollar. GOP sweep: stocks up more than 10%, a 'long AI (NDX), short artificial irrelevance (SPW)' trade.
Tech positioning: investors are max long tech, so BofA would not add. It expects MAGS to beat SOX as growth outperforms cyclicals into the midterms, and finds contrarian China tech interesting.

BofA is 'nibbling' at 'peak yield' plays: GT30, small caps, REITs and HK property. It notes most investors are waiting for a 6% yield to buy Treasuries. Its big-picture view is to stay long gold, commodities and emerging markets.
Equity breadth: 394 stocks trade within 10% of their 52-week high and 206 within 20%, despite S&P 500 all-time highs, which BofA compares to 1999. It expects breadth to improve as yields peak.

Bolsonaro's Brazil win moves LatAm politics to the right: 11 of 20 countries and 420 million people, versus 7 countries and 60 million before. Brazil stocks hit all-time highs and the 10-year yield fell a record 124bps in a day. LatAm equities are still 35% below their all-time high, which BofA calls the best trade to play the US 'Monroe Doctrine'.

Europe is also shifting toward the center-right and far-right (Italy, Germany, Le Pen ahead in France ahead of the Apr 18, 2027 election). A center-right win in the Nov 29 Spanish election is called an underrated positive for euro bonds.
Korean bond yields have risen 200bps in 18 months, and Korea's largest retail broker (Mirae Asset Securities) is down 65% since May. BofA's lesson: 'bonds end bubbles'.

Policy backdrop: government intervention in the economy (a $4bn loan to Vistra, a 10% stake in Trilogy Metals, a $1.5bn loan to Wolfspeed, $2.9bn to Anduril). Europe is considering a levy on US firms with EU revenue above €100mn and limits on Chinese hybrid vehicle imports.

Private clients' cash allocation is 9.4%, a record low, with equities at 66.2% and bonds at 17.1% of $4.6tn AUM. Over four weeks they bought bank loans, industrials and municipal bonds, and sold staples, EM debt and consumer discretionary.

2026 YTD returns: oil +58.5% (WTI +53.7%), US stocks +13.4% (14.9% in the ranked table), global stocks +10.6%, US dollar +3.9%, cash +2.8%, HY -0.5%, IG -3.2%, government bonds -4.4%, gold -4.8%, bitcoin -6.7%. Korea (+98.9%) and Taiwan (+77.4%) equities lead the country table, and India (-15.7%) and China (-12.7%) are at the bottom.

sector_views.rationale: Investors are max long tech, so BofA would not add. Tech saw a $3.5bn weekly inflow, the largest in 6 weeks, and MAGS is expected to beat SOX.
Financials had a $3.0bn weekly outflow, the largest since Mar 2026. Japanese banks tend to outperform when JGB yields rise.
REITs are one of the 'peak yield' plays BofA is nibbling at.
Small caps are one of the 'peak yield' plays BofA is nibbling at, although US small cap funds saw a $1.8bn weekly outflow.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Market-implied odds of a rate hike. BofA says an October hike to cap yields would be among the most bullish 'events' into year-end.
The market prices a high likelihood of a hike by December, consistent with the global tightening cycle BofA flags.
Central banks are tightening for the first time since Sep 2023 (3-month rolling hikes minus cuts), a driver of BofA's risk-off lean.
A high short-term yield sustains money market fund interest income of about $330bn a year and keeps cash on the sidelines.
Approval is near term lows and is raising the odds of a Democratic sweep in the midterms.
The model signals EPS growth rising over the next 6-12 months.

crypto_views: Bitcoin is down 6.7% YTD in the headline scorecard (-4.9% in the ranked FX/commodity table).

tension_points.bull_case: A GOP Senate with a Dem House brings 'gridlock = Goldilocks' and stocks up more than 5%. A GOP sweep could send stocks up more than 10% as the AI boom extends into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic sweep (64% odds) means stocks fall more than 10%, with higher tax and regulation and less ability for Trump to push AI and resource policy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic sweep would invalidate the bullish gridlock case. A Democrat flip of 4 of 6 vulnerable GOP Senate seats (NC, AK, TX, OH, ME, IA) is the path.

tension_points.bull_case: Record cash inflows and $8tn in money market funds is dry powder that could rotate into risk assets.
tension_points.bear_case: Cash stays on the sidelines until big monetary easing or sustained Fed cuts, and with hikes priced, there are no cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Large-scale easing (QE) or sustained Fed rate cuts would release the cash.
